Both species thrive in dense forests and are known for their elusive nature, making them challenging to spot.

articles.title: Study of 500 Ice Age spear points reveals how Clovis hunters managed risk
articles.summary: A fascinating study delved into the projectile points utilized by ancient Clovis and Cumberland cultures in Tennessee, analyzing nearly 500 artifacts from the late Ice Age. Findings reveal that Clovis groups often resharpened their points due to limited resource knowledge, while Cumberland groups tended to discard points with potential still intact. This suggests an evolving approach to resource management, emphasizing the growing familiarity with their environment over generations.

articles.title: Scientists test 16 Asian elephants with hidden fruit; they learn to follow box

Studies indicate that these elephants can switch from direct feeding techniques to indirect methods as needed. While older elephants may find such adaptations more difficult due to slower reflexes, the ability to change tactics is crucial for their social dynamics. This insight into their behavioral flexibility could significantly improve strategies for harmonious coexistence with humans.

articles.title: Pushpak Pujari lost his father in Class 10; how he secured AIR 183 and IIT Delhi

articles.title: Alaska's orange rivers more toxic than mine waste, study finds

Scientists continue monitoring the rivers to understand the long-term impacts of climate change.
